findings.issue_text: [BUG] The deferred import `from sentry.snuba import discover, errors` imports `sentry.snuba.errors`, a module that does not exist in this repository (sentry's error-events dataset module is `sentry.snuba.events`; there is no `src/sentry/snuba/errors.py`). `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` raises ImportError the first time it runs, and it runs unconditionally via `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` at the top of `_get_event_stats`, so every `/organizations/<org>/events-stats/` request (including topEvents) returns a 500 once this code ships.

[BUG] The test module's top-level `from sentry.snuba import discover, errors, transactions` imports the nonexistent `sentry.snuba.errors` module. pytest fails during collection of this file, so all five tests in the diff's only runner-collected test module error before executing, and CI goes red on import failure rather than exercising any of the helper logic.

[BUG] The diff adds a root-level gitlink `sentry-repo` (mode 160000, commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a) with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry and nothing in the PR referencing it. Any `git submodule update --init` or `git clone --recurse-submodules` on this repository fails with `fatal: No url found for submodule path 'sentry-repo' in .gitmodules`, breaking checkouts that recurse submodules; the entry is an unresolvable fabricated path.

[BUG] `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py` is not a path in this repository — sentry's endpoint tests live under `tests/sentry/api/endpoints/` (the diff's own pyproject section registers only `tests.sentry.api.endpoints.*` test modules) — so this hunk modifies a file that does not exist. The new `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` class is never collected by sentry's test runner, so the endpoint-level behavior it appears to verify (upsampled counts of 10, partial-allowlist fallback) ships with zero real coverage, and the patch context of a preexisting 3,549-line file at this path is fabricated against repository reality.

[BUG] The `if dataset == errors: return True` branch compares the passed dataset against the nonexistent `errors` module, so no dataset handle the endpoint actually passes (`sentry.snuba.events`, `discover`, `transactions`, etc.) can ever satisfy it — even after the import above is repaired, the errors-dataset branch is dead code. Error-focused queries run on the events dataset (the endpoint's default) are never upsampled; the transformation only fires via the discover branch with a literal `event.type:error` term, so requests that omit the `dataset` parameter — like the new endpoint tests expecting counts of 10 — stay unupsampled and return raw counts of 1.

[BUG] setUp creates `self.project` and `self.project2` via two bare `self.create_project()` calls, each of which creates a different organization, while every request in the class is issued through `self.project.organization`'s URL with both project IDs as query parameters. The endpoint resolves the project filter within the URL's organization, so project2's event is excluded from the query: `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` gets bucket counts of 10/0 instead of the asserted 10/10, and `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` — whose expected count of 1 depends on non-allowlisted project2 being included — gets 10 because project1 alone is fully allowlisted.

[ADVISORY] The option key `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is read here but is never registered in sentry's options registry anywhere in this diff, and no code path in the diff writes it. Operators cannot populate the allowlist through the options pipeline (options.set rejects unregistered keys), so the feature ships permanently inert and unexercisable outside the mocked tests — anyone attempting the documented rollout finds there is no settable flag to enable it.

[ADVISORY] `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — the only function wired into the production endpoint — has no test anywhere in the diff: the unit-test file imports only the private helpers, and the endpoint tests sit at the uncollected `tests/snuba/` path. The cache-hit short-circuit (`cached_result and ...`), the 60-second TTL, and the allowlist gating ship completely unverified; a regression in cache-key construction or the boolean short-circuit silently alters error counts for allowlisted orgs with no CI signal.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` classifies any query whose raw lowercased string merely contains the substring `event.type:error` — including negations (`-event.type:error`) and incidental mentions inside searched values such as `message:"event.type:error"` — as error-focused. A discover-dataset query that excludes errors or only mentions the token in a value gets its `count()` rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (sum of sample_weight) on allowlisted projects, which errors against transaction rows or returns inflated counts for a query that returns no errors.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has zero call sites anywhere in the diff (nothing invokes it when the allowlist changes), and it hand-duplicates the cache-key f-string from `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. Allowlist changes leave stale eligibility cached for up to 60 seconds with no wired invalidation, and any future edit to one of the two key formats turns the uncalled invalidator into a silent no-op — nothing exercises the pair, so the drift is undetectable until org-wide counts are wrong.

[ADVISORY] The identical gated call `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is duplicated across three separate branches of `_get_event_stats` (top_events, RPC timeseries, legacy timeseries) instead of being computed once before the branching. A future change to the upsampling rewrite in one execution path (e.g., fixing alias or equation handling for the RPC path) leaves the other paths untransformed, producing inconsistent counts between topEvents and regular stats; hoisting a single call above `if top_events > 0:` deletes two of the three sites.

[ADVISORY] `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` adds an unconditional `cache.get` (plus `cache.set` on every miss) to the organization events-stats request path, which previously made no cache calls. The high-QPS dashboard stats endpoint now performs a synchronous Redis roundtrip per request before dispatching to Snuba, adding Redis latency and failover sensitivity to the path's p99 for all orgs, plus a cache SET per (org, project-set) per 60-second window.

[ADVISORY] The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction omits `private=True`, unlike the adjacent internal function in the same `function_converter` list. The experimental aggregate is exposed on the public function surface (function listings/autocomplete served from the converter), letting any org's users execute `upsampled_count()` against projects with no sample_weight guarantees and getting errors or misleading counts, with no documentation or flag gating it.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform tests the `dataset` argument for identity with the sentry.snuba query modules (errors, transactions, discover), but the only wired caller — the `_get_event_stats` closure at organization_events_stats.py:220-222 — passes the endpoint's `Dataset` enum value (that closure keeps the query module in the separate `scoped_dataset` variable), so every comparison is False and the function falls through to `return False` on every request. The upsampling gate always evaluates False, `final_columns` is never rewritten, the feature is dead code through the only endpoint wired in this diff, and test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects (tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py:3626, asserting count == 10) fails with count == 1 — the acceptance criterion the PR exists to meet is satisfied by no code path.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query gates upsampling on a raw substring match (`"event.type:error" in query`), which also matches negated queries like `!event.type:error`, so a query that explicitly excludes errors is classified as error-focused. A chart on allowlisted projects querying `!event.type:error` with yAxis count() has count() rewritten to upsampled_count()/sum(sample_weight) over transaction rows that never carry sample_weight (the helper's own docstring states sample_weight does not exist for transactions), so every bucket returns 0 — or the resolver rejects the column outright — silently zeroing non-error charts instead of returning real counts.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only columns whose lowered text is exactly `count()`, so aliased counts (`count() as raw`) and count() occurrences inside equations pass through untouched while plain `count()` in the same request is upsampled. An allowlisted error chart mixing yAxis values `count()` and `count() as raw` (or an equation referencing count(), which also stays raw via get_equation_list on the topEvents path) renders contradictory series — 10x next to 1x for identical data — with no error signaling the inconsistency, so dashboard consumers cannot tell which number is real.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache ships with no caller anywhere in the diff, and its cache key is built from the exact project-id combination passed in, so even when called it cannot clear the entries written by queries using any other project combination. The module's documented consistency requirement ("should be called when the allowlist configuration changes") is unimplemented — no options-change hook or call site exists — so flipping the allowlist leaves up to 60s of stale mixed upsampled/raw counts, and a maintainer who later wires the invalidator still cannot clear combination-derived keys and will believe the guarantee is enforced.

[ADVISORY] The new unit-test file imports and exercises only the four leaf helpers, omitting is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — the sole function containing the 60s cache read/write and the eligibility/dataset composition — which no test in the diff covers. A regression in cache-key construction (dropping organization.id or the sort of project_ids) silently applies one organization's allowlist eligibility to another organization's queries, and because the endpoint tests never issue two requests to exercise the cache-hit branch, nothing in the suite fails before production dashboards compute counts under the wrong org's configuration.

[ADVISORY] The diff rewrites y_axes/timeseries_columns/selected_columns in four execution branches (top-events RPC, top-events legacy, timeseries RPC, timeseries legacy), but the new endpoint tests issue only plain timeseries requests — none sets topEvents and none enables the RPC path — so three of the four rewritten call sites are never executed by any test. Whether `upsampled_count() as count` survives alias parsing and result serialization through run_top_events_timeseries_query/run_timeseries_query — the RPC path production traffic takes — is unverified, so a parser or result-shape rejection there reaches production as chart failures on every allowlisted organization.

[BUG] test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events sends `dataset: "discover"`, a value the events-stats endpoint rejects (its accepted datasets are the snuba Dataset enum values events/transactions/performance_metrics/metrics_enhanced), so the request returns 400 before any query executes. The test's `assert response.status_code == 200` fails, so the transaction-safety criterion it was written to verify — that transaction events are never upsampled — is never exercised and the behavior ships untested.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a gitlink `sentry-repo` (mode 160000) with no companion .gitmodules entry, leaving the submodule with no URL and unresolvable commit a5d290951de. Every developer or CI job running `git submodule update --init --recursive` (or `git submodule status`) on a fresh checkout fails with 'fatal: no url found for submodule path sentry-repo in .gitmodules', breaking submodule initialization repo-wide.

[ADVISORY] The identical guarded transform `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is hand-duplicated across three execution branches instead of being computed once right after the eligibility gate. Any future change to the transformation (arguments, aliasing, gating condition) must be synchronized in three places, and a miss produces path-dependent behavior where the RPC path upsamples while the legacy path silently returns raw counts — the duplication makes the next change riskier with no branch-specific reason given for the repetition.

[BUG] The diff adds an unexplained `sentry-repo` git submodule (mode 160000) at the repository root that is not traceable to any part of the stated error-upsampling intent. Every clone and CI checkout now materializes an unreviewed external repository at a pinned commit; any code or tooling that scans or imports it picks up supply-chain code nobody on this feature requested, and the submodule's presence is unreviewable scope drift inside a feature PR.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` classifies any query containing the substring 'event.type:error' as error-only, so standard mixed-type discover queries ('event.type:error OR event.type:transaction') and negations ('-event.type:error') trigger the sample_weight transform on transaction rows where the diff itself states sample_weight does not exist. Allowlisted orgs running the common all-events discover query against the stats endpoint get a snuba missing-column failure (500) or garbage counts instead of the raw count() the endpoint promises.

[ADVISORY] `upsampled_count` is registered in the shared discover function registry without `private=True` (unlike the adjacent function it sits next to) and with `default_result_type="number"` while the count() it replaces is integer, exposing an internal rollout helper as a public query function. Any user in any org can now type `upsampled_count()` into arbitrary discover queries; on non-allowlisted projects sample_weight is unpopulated (per the diff's own assumption) so it returns misleading 0 sums, and the number result type serializes upsampled counts as floats (0.0 on zerofill) inconsistently with raw integer counts.

[ADVISORY] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites only the exact token `count()`, so count() occurrences in topEvents equations and display field lists (passed untransformed via `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` and `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)` at organization_events_stats.py:254-256) and aliased forms like `count() as errors` keep raw counts while the y-axis is upsampled. A single allowlisted-org topEvents response mixes upsampled series values (10) with raw equation/field counts (1), rendering internally contradictory widgets.

[ADVISORY] The transform's only safety argument is the docstring's 'no additional null checks are needed' — there is no guard for events ingested before the sampling rollout whose sample_weight is absent or defaulted, so any queried window overlapping pre-enable data mixes raw-weight and 10x-weight events in the same sum. An allowlisted org querying a window that spans the enable date gets silently distorted counts (old events counting as 1 while new ones count as 10, or as 0 if the column defaults to null) with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling transform is wired into exactly one endpoint (organization_events_stats), so the same allowlisted org receives upsampled counts from stats graphs while the events table endpoint, issue stream counts, and every other count()-serving surface still return raw counts for the identical query. Users see a graph showing 10 next to a table showing 1 for the same org, projects, and timeframe, undermining trust in all error counts and generating support load the rollout cannot absorb.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has zero call sites anywhere in the diff — no options-change hook, no signal receiver, not even a test import — so the invalidation contract its docstring documents is unenforceable and the function ships inert. Maintainers reading the docstring believe allowlist changes can be pushed immediately; in reality every allowlist edit rides the 60-second TTL with no override path, and the dead function invites future wiring that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The column transformation is hand-duplicated into three separate pre-execution blocks (lines 232-233, 276-277, 295-296) plus a redundant `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` alias, instead of computing `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` once before the top_events/RPC/standard branch. The next query path added to `_get_event_stats` must remember to copy the `if upsampling_enabled` block or it silently serves raw counts to allowlisted orgs; hoisting the transform deletes two duplicated blocks and the alias outright.

[ADVISORY] All four new endpoint tests exercise only the plain non-RPC timeseries path, leaving the topEvents branch (organization_events_stats.py:229-241) and the use_rpc branch (274-282) — the majority of the new transformation sites — with zero coverage. A regression in those branches, e.g. `upsampled_count` being unresolvable in the top-events or RPC query builders, ships silently and breaks (or silently skips upsampling on) every topEvents/RPC dashboard for allowlisted orgs.

[ADVISORY] The diff includes an unrelated drive-by edit changing the API-visible validation message from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1', which is traceable to no requirement in the upsampling feature. Any client or test asserting the old message breaks, and the unrelated churn obscures the functional diff during review.

[ADVISORY] The 'performance optimization' inserts an unconditional `cache.get` (a Redis round-trip under the production cache backend) plus `cache.set` on expiry into every events-stats request for all orgs, guarding an `options.get` config read that is already served from cached option state. Every dashboard/stats request org-wide pays an added remote cache RTT — including the overwhelmingly common case of orgs that can never be allowlisted — so the optimization adds network work to a hot endpoint rather than removing it.

[BUG] The transform is enabled unconditionally for the errors dataset (`if dataset == errors: return True`) but the `upsampled_count` function is registered only in DiscoverDataset's function_converter (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1041-1052), and per-dataset function registries in this architecture are separate hand-maintained lists — the errors dataset's converter is never given the function. OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint's default dataset is "events" (the errors module), so every default stats query with yAxis=count() for an allowlisted project emits `upsampled_count() as count` into a dataset that cannot resolve the function; the query fails validation and the endpoint returns a query error instead of data — the feature breaks the endpoint's primary path, and the PR's own integration test (test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects, which passes no dataset param) exercises exactly this unregistered path.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query gates the discover-dataset transform on the substring `"event.type:error"` appearing anywhere in the raw query string, so `-event.type:error`, `!event.type:error`, or the token inside a quoted value classify a transaction-only query as error-focused (and error-only discover queries filtered by any other predicate, e.g. issue.id:..., are classified as non-error and left raw). Allowlisted orgs get silently wrong numbers in both directions: a discover chart that excludes errors reports sum(sample_weight) of transaction rows under the label `count`, while error-only charts filtered by anything other than the literal event.type:error keep showing 10x-deflated sampled counts — no error is raised in either case.

[BUG] The diff adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (mode 160000) at the repository root with no .gitmodules entry anywhere in the diff — an unexplained, unresolvable submodule pointer unrelated to the feature. Every clone and CI environment now carries a broken nested-repo entry that cannot be fetched or updated (git submodule operations ignore it because no .gitmodules source exists), committing an accidental nested-clone pointer into the product repo alongside an unrelated feature change.

[ADVISORY] The count()-to-upsampled_count() transformation is wired into exactly one endpoint's `_get_event_stats`, leaving every other count() surface for the same allowlisted projects — organization-events table queries, issues endpoints, and alert/subscription evaluation — on raw sampled counts. Users of allowlisted projects see a dashboard chart report 10x the number its own drill-down table reports for the same bucket; the transformation belongs in the dataset layer (where upsampled_count is registered anyway) so all count() resolution paths answer consistently, and as shipped the product surfaces contradictory numbers for the same query.

[ADVISORY] is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects performs cache.get plus cache.set on every organization-events-stats request — including orgs that can never be allowlisted — to "avoid expensive repeated option lookups", but options.get is already served from Sentry's in-process option cache, so the added layer optimizes an already-cheap lookup while adding two Redis roundtrips per request, one cache key per distinct project combination (unbounded key churn on a hot endpoint), and a new hard dependency on cache availability for a read path that previously never touched the cache. Hot dashboard/alerting traffic pays two extra cache RTTs and per-combination key churn forever to save an in-memory dict lookup — a net latency regression on a top-traffic endpoint, and a cache-backend outage now takes down stats queries that used to succeed.

[ADVISORY] The diff reads the option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` but never registers it (no options.register / REGISTERED_OPTIONS entry anywhere in the diff), and Sentry's supported options write paths validate against the registry. Unless the option is registered in a separate change, operators cannot set the allowlist through the options API or tooling at all — every query takes the `if not allowlist: return False` path and the entire feature ships permanently disabled with no error or signal.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache can only delete the single cache key for the exact (org, project-id-combination) passed, while eligibility is cached under one key per distinct project combination ever queried — a key space that cannot be enumerated — and the function has zero call sites in this diff, so the docstring's promise that calling it on allowlist changes "ensures cache consistency" is unimplementable as designed. The next maintainer who follows the docstring and calls invalidate_upsampling_cache(org, changed_projects) invalidates nothing for every other project combination, leaving queries serving stale allowlist decisions for up to 60 seconds per combination while believing the cache was cleared.

[ADVISORY] The allowlist membership test compares int project ids against raw option contents with no type coercion, and the option is unregistered (hence stored as arbitrary JSON), so an allowlist written as ["123"] never matches project_id 123. An operator enables upsampling for the right projects via the options store and every chart silently stays on raw sampled counts with no error — the write path and the compare path disagree on canonical type (format-drift between what is stored and what is compared).

[ADVISORY] `project_id in allowlist` performs a linear scan of the option list once per project id — O(projects x allowlist size) on every cache miss — instead of a single `set(allowlist)` membership test. Org-wide queries over hundreds of projects against a large allowlist burn the product of both sizes in comparisons inside the request hot path on the events-stats endpoint; the 60-second cache only dampens repeats of the identical combination, not first-seen or diverse dashboard queries.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only the exact token `count()` (case/whitespace-normalized), leaving `count() as <alias>`, `count() as count`, equations embedding count(), and all other aggregates (count_unique, percentiles) untouched while the same request's bare count() is upsampled. A single chart on allowlisted projects silently mixes upsampled and raw series under count-style labels — dashboards that must alias yAxis series (as required when charting multiple count aggregations) or add equations get the pre-feature semantics for half their data with no signal.

[ADVISORY] In the top_events path only y_axes are transformed; the ranking expression `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` (typically count()) and the selected_columns still use raw aggregates, so events are ranked by sampled count while their displayed series are upsampled. For allowlisted projects sampled at 10%, top-N charts select a different event set than a true-count ranking would, and the ranked events' displayed values disagree with the metric that ranked them.

[ADVISORY] The new upsampled_count SnQLFunction declares `default_result_type="number"` (float) while its snql_aggregate wraps the value in toInt64 and the count() it substitutes for is declared "integer" in the same registry. Typed consumers — equation operand validation and any result-type-driven serialization — treat an integer aggregate as a float, so the result metadata for the same logical metric differs depending on whether upsampling applied, and equation type checks can reject compositions that are legal with count().

[ADVISORY] _get_event_stats duplicates the `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` block at three branch sites (top_events at ~232-233, use_rpc at ~276-277, plain path at ~295-296) plus a redundant `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` alias, instead of transforming once before the branching. The next change to the transformation (e.g., also rewriting orderby or count_unique) must be replicated at three hand-maintained sites, and a missed branch silently skips upsampling on that path with no test distinguishing them — hoisting to a single assignment deletes two conditional blocks and the alias.

[BUG] The diff adds an unregistered root-level gitlink 'sentry-repo' (Subproject commit a5d290951de) with no .gitmodules entry, a repo-structure change that is not part of the stated 'upsampled error count' objective. Fresh clones and CI checkouts initialize/fetch an unreviewed external repository into the build (supply-chain exposure and non-reproducible builds), and every developer's `git status` reports the checkout permanently dirty.

[BUG] The 60-second eligibility cache, added under the PR's 'performance optimizations' banner, silently inverts the feature's documented contract: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` (lines 52-55 of this same file) still asserts 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... This is intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state', so two docstrings in one file claim opposite semantics with no accepted decision reconciling them. When an operator removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist to stop inflating counts during an incident, events-stats keeps returning sample_weight-multiplied counts (~10x at client_sample_rate 0.1) for up to 60 more seconds, and the fix for exactly this (invalidate_upsampling_cache) is wired to nothing.

[ADVISORY] is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects performs an unconditional cache.get (plus cache.set on miss) on every organization-events-stats request — including spans/metrics/transactions queries that can never be eligible — replacing the in-process options dict read it claims to optimize with 1-2 synchronous cache-tier round trips, so the 'optimization' makes the hot path slower. Every stats request across all orgs pays added p99 latency and cache-backend load, and the per-(org, project-subset) key writes one entry for every distinct project combination queried — an unbounded high-cardinality key space that evicts useful entries; checking _should_apply_sample_weight_transform (pure local logic) before any cache access would delete all of this remote traffic.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query inspects only request.GET['query'] while _get_event_stats executes the separately-parsed `query` argument it was already handed, so any request whose executed query differs from the raw GET param — the base64 shortQuery form these endpoints accept — bypasses the upsampling gate entirely. Allowlisted projects whose dashboards or saved queries submit shortQuery with event.type:error get raw counts deflated by the client sampling factor (1/10 at 0.1) instead of the upsampled counts the feature exists to provide, with no error surfacing the discrepancy.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling transform rewrites only the y-axis columns, leaving orderby, equations, and groupby on raw count(), so a topEvents request that sorts by count() mixes metrics in one response: the top-N is selected by raw count while the displayed series are upsampled sums. On allowlisted projects a group with 3 events at weight 10 loses to one with 5 events at weight 2 in top-events ranking even though its true upsampled count is 30 vs 10, and equation columns referencing count() stay raw in the same response the user reads as upsampled.

[ADVISORY] The only writer of the sample_rate that drives sample_weight anywhere in this diff is test-factory code (_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling), so the production contract 'sample_rate derives from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate' is established in tests while no production ingestion path in this diff implements it. The endpoint tests assert count==10 using sample_rate fabricated solely by store_event, so the suite stays green if real ingestion never populates sample_rate — in which case upsampled_count() sums sample_weight=1 and silently returns deflated raw counts in production, the exact failure mode these tests exist to catch.

[ADVISORY] The discover gate was 'reduced to only check for event.type:error' per its own docstring, so allowlisted-project queries that omit the explicit filter — which discover still counts errors under — skip upsampling and report error counts deflated by the sampling factor. A user on an allowlisted project who removes the redundant event.type:error term from a saved query watches their error count drop ~10x with no warning, and two dashboards querying the same errors with and without the filter disagree by an order of magnitude — a semantic narrowing granted by the code's own comment rather than any recorded acceptance.

[BUG] The substring check `"event.type:error" in query` matches negated filters, so a discover query of `!event.type:error` — which excludes errors entirely — passes the error-focused gate and gets its y-axis rewritten to sum(sample_weight). On allowlisted projects, a user filtering out errors receives sample_weight sums over the remaining non-error events instead of plain counts — numbers that diverge from count() whenever weights are non-1 — or a hard query failure where the residual events lack a sample_weight column.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff and is never wired to allowlist-option changes, and because eligibility keys are hashed per exact project combination, a single delete can never cover the queries an allowlist change actually affects. The documented contract 'This should be called when the allowlist configuration changes' is unfulfillable as designed — invalidating one (org, project-set) key leaves every other queried subset cached — so operators have no supported way to make a config flip take effect beyond waiting out the 60s TTL.

[ADVISORY] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors dataset, but upsampled_count is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py lines 1041-1052), so the errors path emits a function its resolver cannot resolve. The branch is unreachable from organization-events-stats (whose datasets are discover/transactions/metrics/spans), leaving misleading dead logic; the first future caller that passes the errors dataset to this helper — e.g., an issue-stats integration reusing it — gets an unknown-function query failure (500) instead of upsampled counts.

[ADVISORY] The tests import only the private helpers, so is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — the caching gate the endpoint actually runs — has zero direct coverage of its cache-hit path, the 60s staleness window, or invalidation. A regression in the cache layer (a stuck cached True/False after an allowlist flip, or a key collision across orgs) produces silently wrong counts in production with no failing test, since each e2e test issues at most one request and only ever exercises the cache-miss path.

[ADVISORY] The identical `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` block is hand-copied into three separate query paths (lines ~233, ~278, and here) instead of transforming once before the branching. The next query path added to _get_event_stats — or a refactor touching only one copy — silently serves raw counts on allowlisted projects; a single transform before the branch deletes all three conditionals plus the `upsampling_enabled` alias and `final_columns` initialization.

[ADVISORY] The diff smuggles in an unrelated user-facing change — rewriting the validation error detail 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1' — that has nothing to do with the PR's upsampling objective and was never called out for acceptance. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query gates the discover-dataset transform on the substring `"event.type:error"` appearing anywhere in the raw query string, so `-event.type:error`, `!event.type:error`, or the token inside a quoted value classify a transaction-only query as error-focused (and error-only discover queries filtered by any other predicate, e.g. issue.id:..., are classified as non-error and left raw). Conversely, queries that are effectively error-only without literally containing `event.type:error` (e.g. filtering via other predicates) will be classified as non-error and won’t be transformed. This behavior is directly visible from the diff and can lead to incorrect application (or non-application) of `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects performs cache.get plus cache.set on every organization-events-stats request — including orgs that can never be allowlisted — to "avoid expensive repeated option lookups", but options.get is already served from Sentry's in-process option cache, so the added layer optimizes an already-cheap lookup while adding two Redis roundtrips per request, one cache key per distinct project combination (unbounded key churn on a hot endpoint), and a new hard dependency on cache availability for a read path that previously never touched the cache. adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` unconditionally does `cache.get(cache_key)` on every call, and on a miss does `cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)`. This helper is invoked early in `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats` for every request (before branching on `top_events`/`use_rpc`). That means this hot endpoint now performs external cache operations even when the allowlist is empty / org is not eligible, and it also creates one cache key per distinct `(org, project_ids set)` combination (`hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`), which can churn unboundedly with many project combinations. The parts about options.get already being in-process and cache outages causing request failures aren’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the added cache roundtrips/key churn and new dependency on cache in the read path are clearly diff-grounded performance/architecture concerns rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The allowlist membership test compares int project ids against raw option contents with no type coercion, and the option is unregistered (hence stored as arbitrary JSON), so an allowlist written as ["123"] never matches project_id 123. adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled()` reads `allowlist = options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` and then checks `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `project_id in allowlist` performs a linear scan of the option list once per project id — O(projects x allowlist size) on every cache miss — instead of a single `set(allowlist)` membership test. Org-wide queries over hundreds of projects against a large allowlist burn the product of both sizes in comparisons inside the request hot path on the events-stats endpoint; the 60-second cache only dampens repeats of the identical combination, not first-seen or diverse dashboard queries.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` fetches `allowlist` as a list (`options.get(..., [])`) and then checks `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)`. This is a real, diff-introduced performance issue in a request-path eligibility check (even if dampened by the 60s cache) but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only the exact token `count()` (case/whitespace-normalized), leaving `count() as <alias>`, `count() as count`, equations embedding count(), and all other aggregates (count_unique, percentiles) untouched while the same request's bare count() is upsampled. A single chart on allowlisted projects silently mixes upsampled and raw series under count-style labels — dashboards that must alias yAxis series (as required when charting multiple count aggregations) or add equations get the pre-feature semantics for half their data with no signal.

adjudication.rationale: In `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, the rewrite triggers only when `column.lower().strip() == "count()"`, so any yAxis like `"count() as foo"` (or other count-shaped expressions/equations) will not be transformed. Since `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats` conditionally applies this transform to `query_columns` before executing the query, allowlisted/error queries can return a mix of upsampled series (bare `count()`) and non-upsampled series (aliased/embedded `count()`), silently changing semantics depending on string form within the same request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In the top_events path only y_axes are transformed; the ranking expression `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` (typically count()) and the selected_columns still use raw aggregates, so events are ranked by sampled count while their displayed series are upsampled. For allowlisted projects sampled at 10%, top-N charts select a different event set than a true-count ranking would, and the ranked events' displayed values disagree with the metric that ranked them.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, the new upsampling logic only transforms `query_columns` into `final_columns` and passes that to `y_axes` / `timeseries_columns` / `selected_columns` for the timeseries portions. The top-events ranking inputs (`orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` in both `run_top_events_timeseries_query` and `top_events_timeseries`) and the grouping/selected fields (`selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)`) are not transformed here. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new upsampled_count SnQLFunction declares `default_result_type="number"` (float) while its snql_aggregate wraps the value in toInt64 and the count() it substitutes for is declared "integer" in the same registry. Typed consumers — equation operand validation and any result-type-driven serialization — treat an integer aggregate as a float, so the result metadata for the same logical metric differs depending on whether upsampling applied, and equation type checks can reject compositions that are legal with count().

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`, the new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` defines `snql_aggregate` as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, which produces an integer, but declares `default_result_type="number"`. That creates inconsistent type metadata for the same logical metric when `count()` is replaced with `upsampled_count() as count`, and can plausibly change downstream type-driven behavior (e.g., equation validation/serialization) because the function’s declared result type no longer matches the aggregate’s actual type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _get_event_stats duplicates the `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` block at three branch sites (top_events at ~232-233, use_rpc at ~276-277, plain path at ~295-296) plus a redundant `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` alias, instead of transforming once before the branching. It then conditionally reassigns `final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` in three separate places: inside `if top_events > 0:` before both the RPC (`run_top_events_timeseries_query`) and non-RPC (`top_events_timeseries`) calls, again inside the later `if use_rpc:` (non-top-events) branch before `run_timeseries_query`, and again in the final non-RPC path before `timeseries_query`. This is indeed duplicated, diff-grounded logic that increases maintenance risk if the transformation needs to change or be expanded (would need edits in multiple branches). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 60-second eligibility cache, added under the PR's 'performance optimizations' banner, silently inverts the feature's documented contract: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` (lines 52-55 of this same file) still asserts 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects performs an unconditional cache.get (plus cache.set on miss) on every organization-events-stats request — including spans/metrics/transactions queries that can never be eligible — replacing the in-process options dict read it claims to optimize with 1-2 synchronous cache-tier round trips, so the 'optimization' makes the hot path slower. Every stats request across all orgs pays added p99 latency and cache-backend load, and the per-(org, project-subset) key writes one entry for every distinct project combination queried — an unbounded high-cardinality key space that evicts useful entries; checking _should_apply_sample_weight_transform (pure local logic) before any cache access would delete all of this remote traffic.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, the new code unconditionally calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` before branching on query type/top_events/use_rpc. Inside `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` the first operation is always `cache.get(cache_key)` and on miss `cache.set(...)`, regardless of whether `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` would later return `False` (e.g., `dataset == transactions` or non-error discover queries). This means every org-events-stats request now pays at least one cache access even when upsampling can never apply. Additionally, the cache key includes `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`, which creates entries per distinct project-id combination (potentially high-cardinality/unbounded) as the finding describes. This is a performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query inspects only request.GET['query'] while _get_event_stats executes the separately-parsed `query` argument it was already handed, so any request whose executed query differs from the raw GET param — the base64 shortQuery form these endpoints accept — bypasses the upsampling gate entirely. Allowlisted projects whose dashboards or saved queries submit shortQuery with event.type:error get raw counts deflated by the client sampling factor (1/10 at 0.1) instead of the upsampled counts the feature exists to provide, with no error surfacing the discrepancy.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, the executed query string is the already-parsed `query` argument passed into Snuba (`query_string=query` / `user_query=query`). But the new upsampling gate `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` does not take that `query` value; instead it calls `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)`, which for the discover dataset calls `_is_error_focused_query(request)` and inspects only `request.GET.get("query", "")`. This creates a real correctness mismatch whenever the effective executed query differs from the raw `GET['query']` (e.g., if the endpoint supports alternate encodings/parameters or the server rewrites/parses the query before passing it as `query`). In such cases the upsampling decision can be wrong (skip upsampling even though the executed query is error-focused), producing incorrect counts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The upsampling transform rewrites only the y-axis columns, leaving orderby, equations, and groupby on raw count(), so a topEvents request that sorts by count() mixes metrics in one response: the top-N is selected by raw count while the displayed series are upsampled sums. On allowlisted projects a group with 3 events at weight 10 loses to one with 5 events at weight 2 in top-events ranking even though its true upsampled count is 30 vs 10, and equation columns referencing count() stay raw in the same response the user reads as upsampled.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats.py`, the upsampling logic only rewrites `query_columns` into `final_columns` and then uses that only for `y_axes`/`timeseries_columns`/`selected_columns` (e.g. `run_top_events_timeseries_query(... y_axes=final_columns ...)`, `top_events_timeseries(timeseries_columns=final_columns, ...)`, `run_timeseries_query(... y_axes=final_columns ...)`, `timeseries_query(selected_columns=final_columns, ...)`). However, the same requests still pass unmodified `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` and `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` and `raw_groupby=self.get_field_list(...)`. Since `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites literal `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count`, any equations that reference `count()` are not transformed and can remain based on raw counts while the displayed y-axis series is upsampled. Likewise, ordering/top-N selection can be inconsistent if ordering is based on a raw `count()` expression rather than the rewritten aggregation. This is a correctness issue exposed by the diff’s partial transformation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only writer of the sample_rate that drives sample_weight anywhere in this diff is test-factory code (_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling), so the production contract 'sample_rate derives from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate' is established in tests while no production ingestion path in this diff implements it. The endpoint tests assert count==10 using sample_rate fabricated solely by store_event, so the suite stays green if real ingestion never populates sample_rate — in which case upsampled_count() sums sample_weight=1 and silently returns deflated raw counts in production, the exact failure mode these tests exist to catch.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the only newly added path that derives `sample_rate` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` is in test infrastructure (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` added to `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py` and invoked in `Factories.store_event`). The production-side changes for upsampling (`upsampled_count()` in `discover.py` and the `count()`→`upsampled_count()` rewrite in `organization_events_stats.py` via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`) do not include any ingestion/population logic for `sample_rate`/`sample_weight`. The new endpoint tests asserting `count == 10` depend on `store_event` injecting `sample_rate`, so they would not catch a real-world scenario where production ingestion fails to populate the needed field(s). The diff doesn’t prove production ingestion is missing this mapping globally, but it does show the tests are establishing that contract only via the factory, which is a valid review concern about test fidelity rather than a directly verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The discover gate was 'reduced to only check for event.type:error' per its own docstring, so allowlisted-project queries that omit the explicit filter — which discover still counts errors under — skip upsampling and report error counts deflated by the sampling factor. A user on an allowlisted project who removes the redundant event.type:error term from a saved query watches their error count drop ~10x with no warning, and two dashboards querying the same errors with and without the filter disagree by an order of magnitude — a semantic narrowing granted by the code's own comment rather than any recorded acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-gates upsampling for the discover dataset on an explicit substring check for `event.type:error` (see `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` calling `_is_error_focused_query()`, and `_is_error_focused_query()` only returning True when `"event.type:error"` is present in `request.GET["query"]`). As a result, even if the discover dataset query ends up counting error events via other/default semantics, the new upsampling transform will not be applied unless that exact filter is included, which can create inconsistent counts between otherwise-similar queries. Whether discover actually returns errors without that filter isn’t provable from this diff alone, so this is flagged as a scope/semantic risk introduced by the change rather than a definitively verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The substring check `"event.type:error" in query` matches negated filters, so a discover query of `!event.type:error` — which excludes errors entirely — passes the error-focused gate and gets its y-axis rewritten to sum(sample_weight). On allowlisted projects, a user filtering out errors receives sample_weight sums over the remaining non-error events instead of plain counts — numbers that diverge from count() whenever weights are non-1 — or a hard query failure where the residual events lack a sample_weight column.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `"event.type:error"` (via `if "event.type:error" in query:`). This will also match negated filters like `!event.type:error`, incorrectly treating an "exclude errors" discover query as error-focused. That feeds into `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` for the `discover` dataset and then into `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, enabling `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` to rewrite `count()` to `upsampled_count()` in `organization_events_stats.py`. Since the code explicitly states `sample_weight` doesn't exist for transactions, this can produce incorrect counts or query failures when the remaining (non-error) events lack `sample_weight`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff and is never wired to allowlist-option changes, and because eligibility keys are hashed per exact project combination, a single delete can never cover the queries an allowlist change actually affects.
